description: Evaluation benchmarks for tactical equity rotation, macro regime detection, and evidence-backed inflection signals

cases.prompt: FII Index Futures Long/Short ratio has fallen to 15%, but Nifty is holding its 200-DMA and PCR is 1.45. What tactical sector rotation should I make over the next 3 to 5 trading days?
expected_criteria: Identifies extreme institutional oversold positioning (FII Longs at 15%) vulnerable to an imminent short squeeze
Confirms high Put-Call Ratio (1.45) as institutional put writing support floor
Recommends tactical rotation into high-beta Banking & Financials (Nifty Bank / Private Banks) to capture the squeeze
Specifies invalidation level if Nifty breaks key technical support on heavy cash volumes

cases.prompt: Leading economic indicators show domestic manufacturing growth slowing down, while food and oil prices are pushing inflation higher. India VIX has jumped to 21. How should I rotate my equity sectors?
expected_criteria: Diagnoses Quadrant 3: Late Cycle (decelerating growth, rising inflation)
Recommends trimming high-beta cyclicals (Metals, high-debt Real Estate) by 10%
Recommends overweighting Defensives with domestic pricing power (Nifty FMCG, Nifty Pharma & Healthcare)
Preserves 70% core buy-and-hold foundation and caps tactical rotation within 20%-30% satellite bucket

cases.prompt: The Nifty Smallcap 250 index P/E is currently 31.0, while the Nifty 50 P/E is 23.5 (ratio = 1.32x). Market breadth is showing only 41% of stocks above their 50-DMA despite headline indices at record highs. What is the evidence-backed recommendation?
expected_criteria: Highlights severe valuation froth with Smallcap-to-Largecap PE ratio > 1.25x
Flags market breadth divergence (less than 45% of stocks above 50-DMA while index makes highs)
Mandates a 25% to 35% tactical trim of Smallcap mutual funds
Reallocates proceeds into Large-Cap Quality, Flexi-Cap, or Sovereign Gold Bonds

cases.prompt: The Bank of England and Federal Reserve have initiated their rate-cutting cycle while manufacturing PMIs are rebounding from contraction into expansion territory. What is the tactical sector rotation playbook?
expected_criteria: Classifies macro regime as Quadrant 1: Early Cycle (accelerating growth, falling rates)
Recommends rotating from defensive utilities/staples into growth and cyclicals (Global Tech, Consumer Discretionary, Industrials)
Advises executing trades inside UK Stocks & Shares ISA to maintain 0% Capital Gains Tax friction
Provides concrete leading triggers and invalidation metrics

cases.capability: Tax-Smart Mutual Fund Rotation in India
cases.prompt: I want to rotate between sectors regularly in India, but I am worried about the 20% Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) tax on units held under 1 year. How can I implement tactical rotations tax-efficiently?
expected_criteria: Calculates the severe performance drag of paying 20% STCG or 12.5% LTCG on frequent fund switches
Recommends Balanced Advantage Funds (BAFs) / Dynamic Asset Allocation Funds where internal asset and sector rotation is 100% tax-free to the investor
Suggests Multi-Asset Allocation Funds for rotating across Equities, Debt, and Gold with zero personal tax trigger until final redemption
Maintains a strict Core (70% passive/flexicap) and Satellite (30% tactical) portfolio split

cases.prompt: I am a higher-rate taxpayer in London with £100k in my Stocks & Shares ISA and £50k in a General Investment Account (GIA). I want to execute tactical sector rotations. Which account should I use?
expected_criteria: Mandates concentrating all active tactical sector rotations strictly inside the Stocks & Shares ISA (100% exempt from CGT and dividend tax)
Warns against active sector churn in the taxable GIA due to the small £3,000 annual exemption and 24% CGT rate
Advises leaving the taxable GIA in passive, buy-and-hold low-turnover global index funds to minimize taxable realization events
